chapter.heading: International Fame
chapter.v:
When Hiram
king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king to succeed his father, he sent ambassadors to Solomon because Hiram had always been David's friend.

So Solomon
sent this message back to Hiram,

“As you
know, my father David was not able to build a Temple to honor the Lord his God because of the wars fought against him from every direction, until the Lord had conquered his enemies.

But now
the Lord my God has given me peace all around—no enemies, no bad things happening.

So I
plan to build a Temple to honor the Lord my God, as the Lord told my father David. He said to him, ‘Your son whom I will place on your throne to succeed you will build the Temple to honor me.’

So please
order some cedars of Lebanon to be cut down for me. My workers will assist your workers, and I will pay your workers at the rate that you decide, for you know that we don't have anyone who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”

When Hiram
heard Solomon's message, he was very happy and said, “Praise the Lord today, for he has given David a wise son to lead this great nation!”

Hiram sent
this reply to Solomon:“Thank you for your message. As for the cedar and cypress timber, I will do everything you want.

My workers
will bring the logs down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will have them floated in rafts by sea to wherever you decide. I will have the rafts broken apart there, and you can take the logs away. In return I would like you to provide food for my household.”

So Hiram
provided Solomon with as much cedar and cypress timber as he wanted,

Solomon gave
Hiram 20,000 cors of wheat for food and 20,000 cors of olive oil for his household. Solomon provided this to Hiram every year.

The Lord
gave Solomon wisdom just as he had promised him. Hiram and Solomon had a good relationship and they made a peace treaty with each other.
chapter.heading: The Temple Work Begins
chapter.v:
King Solomon
drafted a labor force of 30,000 from all of Israel.

He sent
them in shifts of 10,000 each month to Lebanon, so that they were one month in Lebanon and two months at home, Adoniram was in charge of the labor force.

Solomon had
70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the hill country,

as well
as 3,300 foremen he placed in charge of the workers.

Following the
king's orders, they quarried large blocks of stone that were expensive to produce, and laid these dressed stones as the foundation for the Temple.

So Solomon's
and Hiram's builders, together with the Gebalites, cut the stone. They prepared the timber and stone to build the Temple.
